title: Irregular Natural Flagstone Re-Installation - Bates Landscaping
text: The Event Venue Representative had safety concerns on the patio that their guests use for their weddings.

Bates Landscaping recommended the replacement of the base material that is under the patio and replacement of broken stone pieces, to secure and make safe for all guests. We pulled up sections of the natural cleft flagstone patio and removed the existing base that was in poor condition. We removed stumps and old decayed roots that were causing sinking in certain areas. We removed any hazardous, broken pieces of flagstone, and replaced it with new sturdy pieces. We re-install the new, proper stone, sand, and liner base for the patio, and re-installed the flagstone. Lastly we applied polysand throughout to secure and seal.

title: Native Planting with Added Water Feature - Bates Landscaping
text: Native Planting with Added Water Feature
The client has acreage that they wanted to convert from turf to a native, wildlife garden.

We did a site survey and located approximately a quarter acre that we proposed clusters of planting beds with turf walking paths meandering between. We added a small pond with a bubbler to provide a wildlife drinking source. We chose a palette of all native plantings cultivated in coordination with the client to attract particular wildlife while maintaining four seasons of interest.

We presented the client options for a structural planting more focused on trees and shrubs and also presented the option to add a significant amount of native grasses and perennials which the client chose. We finally added a grassy swale and a rain garden to support drainage in the site.

title: Storm Water Drainage with Berms and Piping - Bates Landscaping
text: Storm Water Drainage with Berms and Piping
The client has a property in a valley that received 41 inches of water in the lower floor during a hurricane.

We began by addressing where the water flow was breaching the property by site surveys and topographical mapping. We proposed a system of large berms and swales with a commercial sized channel drain across the driveway and presented an option to use commercial sized concrete storm drains and 12” piping to supplement the berm and swale system.

The client chose to add the concrete storm drains and piping so that the berms could be lowered while still allowing for large scale drainage volume. We also added in drainage and redid hardscape along lower lying areas that had previously been damaged by the flooding.

title: Bamboo Removal - Bates Landscaping
text: The homeowners called Bates Landscaping for the removal of their bamboo. The bamboo was spreading from a neighboring property, and although they enjoyed it, it was crowding into the lawn space.
The homeowners called Bates Landscaping for the removal of their bamboo. The bamboo was spreading from a neighboring property, and although they enjoyed it, it was crowding into the lawn space.

We recommended the complete removal of the bamboo, by cutting down all the shoots first. Then we brought in equipment to dig out and remove all the rhizomes (roots of the bamboo). We hauled all of the roots away and disposed of them properly. Then we used different equipment to create a final grade to match the remainder of the property.
A barrier is typically suggested because the bamboo remains on the neighboring properties, but this homeowner opted to simply maintain it with regular mowing, if it creeps back under the fence.

title: Bamboo Removal - Bates Landscaping
text: The Property Manager and Board Members of this Community reached out to Bates for a solution on their bamboo that borders a portion of the development. Being that this was a capital improvement project for them, they wanted the most cost-effective option – they also love the privacy it provides from the newly constructed community behind them.

The Property Manager and Board Members of this Community reached out to Bates for a solution on their bamboo that borders a portion of the development. Being that this was a capital improvement project for them, they wanted the most cost-effective option – they also love the privacy it provides from the newly constructed community behind them.

Bates recommended a cut down / back approach to the community with on-going maintenance of mowing. The bamboo measured at 250ft long and we pushed it back by 15ft into the woods. This would allow homeowners within the community to gain an additional 15ft of lawn space, while also slowing down the growth of the bamboo.

Bates did not dig out the rhizomes (bamboo roots) in an effort to reduce costs for the community. The development is also to mow the small shoots down now with regular weekly mowing to keep it in better condition for the nearby homeowners.

title: Drainage Issue + Water in Home - Bates Landscaping
text: The homeowners asked Bates to solve a few issues for them at their beautiful home in Chester County. First, the outdated and failing retaining wall at the driveway – second, the failing railroad tie wall at the front foundation, and third the water issues!

The homeowners asked Bates to solve a few issues for them at their beautiful home in Chester County. First, the outdated and failing retaining wall at the driveway – second, the failing railroad tie wall at the front foundation, and third the water issues!

Bates customized a stormwater solution that started before the rainwater even enters the property! We created a berm along the edge of the road to continue the flow of water at the street, as the road was constructed for. After that, we contoured the front lawn area to move water into strategically placed catch basins that channel water into the lower part of the back yard.

Bates also reconstructed the outdated timber walls at the front foundation and along the driveway. These were replaced with beautifully sourced PA boulders to maintain the natural appearance of the surrounding areas. The steps were installed with a tier placement to allow easy access for family members at the lower part of the driveway!
